method: A standard pipe offset turns the run once through the fitting angle. The calculator takes the offset as the perpendicular distance between the two pipe centre lines, then divides it by the sine of the fitting angle for the travel, the centre-to-centre distance along the diagonal, and by the tangent of that angle for the run, the distance the pipe advances along its original axis. The travel is the hypotenuse of the offset and the run, so the two legs come back exactly as offset divided by travel and run divided by travel: those are the sine and the cosine of the fitting angle. A rolling offset enters a vertical and a horizontal set instead. The true offset is their hypotenuse, and the roll angle is atan2 of the vertical leg over the horizontal one, measured from the horizontal leg towards the vertical one, so a horizontal-only set reads 0 degrees and a vertical-only set reads 90. The cut length is the travel less each fitting's centre-to-face take-out, entered per fitting because the two ends need not match. Units are labels only: no number is converted, and the page sends, stores and uploads nothing. It refuses an offset that is blank, non-numeric or not greater than zero, a rolling offset with both legs zero, a fitting angle outside 1 to 89 degrees, a negative take-out, and a pair of take-outs that adds up to more than the travel, naming the field in each message.
